prompt.context: Our client is Amusement Worldwide, an international amusement park company. Amusement Worldwide owns and operates dozens of parks around the world. These parks are regional parks, where visitors drive to the park for the day and not resort destinations, to which visitors travel great distances. Amusement Worldwide has been quite successful recently and is looking to grow inorganically, with a budget of up to $1.5B. We've been hired to evaluate whether or not they should acquire a local amusement park called Thrill Park, which is very popular in a region in which Amusement Worldwide is not currently present.
prompt.question: What are the important considerations when evaluating Thrill Park?

clarifying_info.a: Thrill Park is a single park in North Carolina and is privately owned.

clarifying_info.q: What type of guests does Thrill Park serve?
clarifying_info.a: It caters to guests of all ages with attractions ranging from simple shows and rides for young children to extreme rollercoasters for adults — similar to current Amusement Worldwide parks.

clarifying_info.q: Why is Amusement Worldwide looking to acquire?
clarifying_info.a: Amusement Worldwide has excess cash on hand and would like to make a positive investment.

clarifying_info.q: Can we get financial data from Thrill Park?
clarifying_info.a: We can't get detailed financial/operating data from Thrill Park, but Amusement Worldwide has lots of experience in this space and can provide estimates.

clarifying_info.q: How many days per year is Thrill Park open?
clarifying_info.a: The park is open 150 days a year (seasonal).

clarifying_info.q: What is the profit margin on merchandise?
clarifying_info.a: The profit margin on merchandise is two thirds (67%).

exhibits.title: Estimated Daily Visitors to Thrill Park
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing estimated daily visitors (in thousands) to Thrill Park by month from March through October, with individual day-of-week bars. Average daily attendance is labeled as 10 thousand visitors.

data.y_axis: Estimated daily visitors, thousands (0 to 150 scale)

framework: Valuation of Thrill Park as a standalone asset (revenue, costs, profit, DCF)
Revenue streams: ticket sales, food/concessions, merchandise
Synergies available to Amusement Worldwide (revenue and cost)
Strategic fit: geographic expansion, brand, competitive positioning
Acquisition premium and whether total value justifies the price
Risks: projection accuracy, brand dilution, capital alternatives, asset condition

questions.prompt: Calculate the total annual revenue from ticket sales.
questions.guidance: Use average daily visitors (10,000) times days open per year (150) to get annual visitors, then multiply by the entrance fee ($50). Strong candidates read the exhibit correctly and note the average of 10k/day.

math.setup: Annual visitors = average daily visitors x days open; Ticket revenue = annual visitors x price per ticket

questions.prompt: Given the following additional data, calculate the annual profit for Thrill Park: operating costs = $60M/yr; average guest spends $20/day on food with 50% profit margin; 25% of guests are collectors spending $36 on merchandise, 75% are casual guests spending $12 on merchandise (merchandise margin = 67%).
questions.guidance: Candidate must calculate three profit streams: (1) ticket profit = ticket revenue minus operating costs; (2) food profit = food revenue x margin; (3) merchandise profit = blended merchandise revenue x margin. Then sum all three.

math.setup: Ticket profit = ticket revenue - operating costs; Food profit = food revenue x 50%; Merchandise profit = blended merchandise revenue x 67%
steps: Food revenue: $20 x 1,500,000 = $30M; Food profit: $30M x 50% = $15M
Merchandise revenue per guest: ($36 x 25%) + ($12 x 75%) = $9 + $9 = $18/guest
Total merchandise revenue: $18 x 1,500,000 = $27M; Merchandise profit: $27M x 67% = $18M

questions.prompt: What is the fair value of Thrill Park if profit grows at 3% per year and the discount rate is 8%?
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply the growing perpetuity (Gordon Growth) formula: Value = Cash Flow / (discount rate - growth rate). Strong candidates recall this formula quickly and apply it cleanly.

math.setup: Growing perpetuity value = Annual profit / (discount rate - growth rate)

questions.prompt: What are some other factors Amusement Worldwide should consider when deciding to buy Thrill Park?
questions.guidance: This is a brainstorming question. Strong answers note: (1) an acquisition premium will likely be paid above intrinsic value, which must be recovered through synergies; (2) revenue and cost synergies available to AW; (3) risks such as hurting the Thrill Park brand, better alternatives for the capital, and inaccurate projections. Other considerations: age/condition of rides and equipment, local competitors, branding and consolidation benefits.

questions.prompt: Amusement Worldwide believes it could increase ticket sales by 10%, cut operating costs by 5%, and cut the cost of food by 10% (no merchandise savings due to existing supplier contract). What is the total economic benefit (NPV of synergies) of Amusement Worldwide owning Thrill Park?
questions.guidance: Candidate must calculate three synergy streams, then capitalize them as a perpetuity using the same 3%/8% growth/discount rates. Assume synergies fully realized in year 1.

math.setup: Revenue synergy = ticket revenue x 10%; Operating cost synergy = operating costs x 5%; Food cost synergy = food cost (not food revenue) x 10%; NPV of synergies = total annual synergies / (discount rate - growth rate)
steps: Food cost synergy: food cost = $30M revenue - $15M profit = $15M cost; $15M x 10% = $1.5M

questions.prompt: Thrill Park has offered to sell itself for $1.1B (a premium of $140M over the $960M standalone value). Should Amusement Worldwide accept this offer?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compare total value to Amusement Worldwide ($960M standalone + $240M synergies = $1.2B) against the asking price ($1.1B). Since $1.1B < $1.2B, and the $140M premium is less than the $240M in synergy value, the acquisition creates value. A strong answer also notes risks and the budget cap of $1.5B is not exceeded.

math.setup: Total value to AW = standalone value + NPV of synergies; Compare to asking price
steps: Premium paid: $140M vs. synergy value $240M — premium is justified
math.answer: Yes, accept the offer; Thrill Park is worth $1.2B to AW, so the $1.1B price creates $100M of value

questions.prompt: (Optional) How many guests per year does Thrill Park need to attract to break even?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate the per-guest contribution margin across all revenue streams, then divide fixed operating costs by that margin. Food contribution = $10/guest (50% of $20). Merchandise contribution uses blended average = $18/guest x 67% = ~$12/guest.

math.setup: Profit per guest = ticket price + food contribution + merchandise contribution; Breakeven guests = fixed costs / profit per guest
math.answer: ~833,000 guests per year to break even

brainstorming.prompt: What are some additional ways that Thrill Park could potentially become more profitable?

categories.name: Current Operations
ideas: Get local or national sponsorships and suppliers
Open for more days per year
Invest in more marketing to drive attendance
Dynamic or surge pricing on peak days

categories.name: New Revenue Streams
ideas: Change business model — open a hotel or resort to capture overnight guests
Offer season tickets, bundled packages, or family memberships
Add new rides or attractions to boost attendance and willingness to pay
Offer VIP experiences or private event rentals

recommendation: Amusement Worldwide should acquire Thrill Park at the offered price of $1.1B
The standalone DCF value is $960M and AW-specific synergies add $240M, making Thrill Park worth $1.2B to the client — $100M above the asking price
The deal fits within the $1.5B budget and provides a foothold in a new geographic region
risks: Projections and estimates may be inaccurate — actual attendance or margins could disappoint
Acquisition integration could damage the Thrill Park brand or culture
Age and condition of rides/equipment may require significant capital reinvestment
There may be better uses of the $1.1B budget (alternative acquisitions or organic growth)
A local competitor in North Carolina could erode future attendance
next_steps: Conduct full due diligence on Thrill Park financials, asset condition, and legal/regulatory matters
Assess competitive landscape in the North Carolina region
Develop a detailed integration plan to realize the $12M/yr synergy target
Finalize deal structure and negotiate terms with Thrill Park owners
